A.explanation: This is $0.15 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 0.075 \text{ N}$, which incorrectly uses $\sin$ for the horizontal to vertical ratio instead of $\tan$.

B.explanation: Horizontal air force balances the horizontal component of tension while weight balances the vertical component, giving $F = W \tan 30^{\circ} = 0.087 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: This is $0.15 / \tan 30^{\circ} = 0.26 \text{ N}$, which inverts the triangle and divides by $\tan 30^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying.

D.explanation: This is $0.15 / \sin 30^{\circ} = 0.30 \text{ N}$, which is the tension in the string, not the horizontal force from the air flow.

hints: Notice the three forces on the ball: weight $0.15 \text{ N}$ vertically down, air force horizontally, and tension along the string at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical.
For equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so the horizontal and vertical components of tension must separately balance the air force and the weight.
Write $T\cos 30^{\circ} = 0.15 \text{ N}$ and $T\sin 30^{\circ} = F$ and divide the equations to eliminate $T$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces: weight $W = 0.15 \text{ N}$ down, unknown horizontal force $F$ from the air flow, and tension $T$ at $30^{\circ}$ from the vertical.
Resolve tension: vertical component is $T\cos 30^{\circ}$ upward and horizontal component is $T\sin 30^{\circ}$ opposite to the air flow.
Apply equilibrium: net vertical force is zero so $T\cos 30^{\circ} = W$, and net horizontal force is zero so $T\sin 30^{\circ} = F$.
Substitute values with units: $F = 0.15 \times \tan 30^{\circ} = 0.15 \times 0.577 = 0.0866 \text{ N} \approx 0.087 \text{ N}$.
